|quest_reward4_act = 6 |quest_reward4_npc = Lilly Roth }} '''Bear Trap''' throws a [[trap]] that deals physical damage to the enemy that triggered it and applies a debuff that greatly reduces [[movement speed]] and causes them to take increased damage from traps and [[mine]]s. ==Skill functions and interactions== * '''Secondary damage''': Bear Traps deals [[secondary damage]]. It doesn't benefit from [[modifier]]s to [[spell]]s and [[attack]]s, and therefore cannot be [[block]]ed/[[spell block]]ed or [[dodge]]d/[[spell dodge]]d. * '''Duration''': The base [[duration]] of the immobilization effect is 150ms per % of enemy max [[life]] dealt as [[damage]], to a maximum of 1/3 of max life. Modifiers to skill duration alter both the lifetime of the trap and the duration of the immobilization. This immobilization is not considered a [[stun]], and will not interact with modifiers that affect stuns. ==Gem level progression== {{Skill progression |c1_abbr = Physical

The debuff lingers for a duration after the immobilising effects wear off. While debuffed, enemies take 15% increased damage from traps and mines, and have 80% less movement speed. This movement speed gradually recovers back to normal over the course of the debuff's duration * Now has a 4 second cooldown (up from 3). * Mana cost has been lowered at all levels. Now costs 6 mana at gem level 1 (down from 11), up to 23 mana at gem level 20 (down from 46) * Now has a base critical strike chance of 6% (up from 5%). }} {{Version history table row|3.2.0| * Base duration lowered to 8 seconds (from 16). }} {{Version history table row|3.1.0| * Bear Trap and {{il|Vaal Rain of Arrows}} now remove all movement speed, as opposed to reducing it by 300%. }} {{Version history table row|2.0.0| * Now grants 1% increased physical damage per 1% quality (up from 0.75% per 1% quality). }} {{Version history table row|1.0.0| * Damage at high levels has been reduced by around 40% at level 15. }} {{Version history table row|0.10.5| * Bear Trap's damage has been increased at lower levels and reduced at higher levels.
